claims.text: High-entropy alloys contain multiple principal elements and have a wide range of possible compositions.
Machine-learning algorithms can effectively predict optimal HEA compositions.
Machine learning can design refractory HEAs that are intrinsically strong.
Machine learning can design refractory HEAs that are ductile.
Machine learning can design refractory HEAs that are low in weight.
Machine-learning algorithms analyze existing alloy-composition and property data.
Machine learning identifies patterns linking alloy composition with desired mechanical characteristics.
Machine-learning-predicted compositions will exhibit improved strength.
Machine-learning-predicted compositions will exhibit improved ductility.
Machine-learning-predicted compositions will have reduced weight.
Machine-learning-predicted compositions will maintain refractory properties.
Thermo-kinetic analysis and simulation are less efficient than machine learning at determining optimal HEA compositions.
The proposed method is limited in scope to high-entropy alloys.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis asserts that machine learning can effectively predict optimal compositions, while the uncertainty field states that effectiveness is uncertain because no specific empirical evidence supports the application.
